limitations: The 0.992 m vertex grid cannot resolve sub-metre blocks, cracks or texture.
Slope and especially curvature amplify height quantisation, interpolation and classification noise.
DTM is bare-earth geometry and does not identify rock, grass, scree, paths, vegetation or wetness.
Roughness is scale-dependent geometric evidence, not a material classification.
Square-window roughness is undefined near edges by half the window width.

curvature.laplacian: d2z/dx2 + d2z/dy2; positive hollow/concave, negative ridge/convex
curvature.plan: horizontal contour curvature; positive concave/hollow, negative convex/ridge
curvature.profile: normal curvature in the downslope gradient direction; positive concave-up, negative convex-up

roughness.algorithm: RMS vertical residual after least-squares local plane removal in a centred square window
roughness.edge_and_nodata_policy: NODATA unless the full window contains valid samples

semantic_invariants: Mapped bedrock does not imply exposed rock.
No mapped superficial deposit does not prove bare bedrock.
Low NDVI, steep terrain, or rough terrain alone do not imply rock.
Historical habitat does not imply unchanged current habitat.
Dated Sentinel state does not become timeless surface identity.
Alignment grid spacing is not source information resolution.
Probabilities do not identify rocks, fractures, vegetation objects, textures, or square-metre material truth.
Source disagreement remains evidence rather than being treated as source error.
